scope: Native NtSetTimer2/NtCancelTimer2 semantics for existing extended IRTimer objects and actual scheduler/wait integration. Ordinary Windows next frontier is measured, not substituted.
acceptance: Capture independent native set/cancel/state/fault/access/guard/lifecycle behavior on ARM64, x64 compatibility, x86 and x86 LAA.

Support exact guest arm, reset, periodic expiry and cancellation state with precise units; existing wait-any/all, notification/synchronization, native wait and wait-packet consumers observe the same object.
Preserve existing NtCreateTimer2 construction, legacy timers, synthetic NTDLL ordinals/trap RVAs, C ABI and defaults.
Baseline strategic tests fail before product changes; all code changes precede final test gates.
Complete affected library targets and all-target checks plus CAPI and actual retained consumers on macOS/Linux/Windows; ordinary programs execute normally against rebuilt owning core.
Publish exact semantic owned paths with red, push RAX master and pair root pin/records to both remotes; no merge commits.

assumptions.assumption: The existing Object::IrTimer represents the extended kernel timer used by the observed NtSetTimer2 call.
assumptions.basis: Guest trace: handle0x2c, attributes8, timer_idNone, dormant signal; independent native exact request succeeds. Existing NtCreateTimer2 implementation records all extended types as IrTimer.
assumptions.dependent-result: Add real arming/cancellation state to this object rather than legacy Object::Timer.
assumptions.stress-test: Native regular/extended/event/invalid handles, all supported constructor attribute families and access grants.
assumptions.falsification-probe: Native NtSetTimer2 accepts a different dispatcher object or existing constructor representation disagrees with native type capture.

assumptions.assumption: Version/Reserved/NoWakeTolerance layout is two ULONGs plus LONGLONG in16bytes.
assumptions.basis: Stored pinned PHNT ntexapi.h lines1373-1394 and exact native ctypes sizeof16 success.
assumptions.dependent-result: Input capture, cross-ABI parsing and time-unit model.
assumptions.stress-test: All pointer alignments, crossing/guard/noaccess pages, nonzero version/reserved, boundary tolerance values; WoW64 fault ordering.
assumptions.falsification-probe: Native captures use different offsets/size or branch semantics than the declaration.

assumptions.assumption: All native test operations remain confined to anonymous handles in their own producer processes.
assumptions.basis: Fixed creation API, no object names, no host policy writes and unconditional cancellation/close cleanup.
assumptions.stress-test: Check handle counts, guard regions, before/after module and producer hashes; avoid unbounded waits.
assumptions.falsification-probe: Handle leak, non-private target, global policy mutation or an unbounded wait.
